newsitem.title: USA: NFL-COWBOYS' IRVIN, WILLIAMS SETTLE DEFAMATION SUIT.
newsitem.headline: NFL-COWBOYS' IRVIN, WILLIAMS SETTLE DEFAMATION SUIT.

text.p: Dallas Cowboys stars Michael Irvin and Erik Williams have settled a defamation lawsuit against a Dallas television station for reporting false sexual assault allegations against them, officials said Wednesday.

Attorneys for the players and officials at KXAS-TV said they had reached an out-of-court settlement but declined to give details. Unconfirmed radio reports said the two players each would receive $1 million from the station.
A local topless dancer named Nina Shahravan accused Irvin and Williams of sexually assaulting her at gunpoint late last year and KXAS-TV reporter Marty Griffin broke the story.
The players' attorneys claimed Griffin had jumped to accuse Irvin and Williams even as evidence emerged that Shahravan was lying.
Dallas police cleared the players after an 11-day investigation and Shahravan faces charges of perjury.

Irvin and Williams have also filed a separate federal lawsuit against the City of Dallas and five Dallas police officers for allegedly violating their civil rights in handling the highly publicised case.
Irvin, a wide receiver, and Williams, an offensive lineman, are both All-Pros and played key roles in the Cowboys' three Super Bowl victories in the 1990s.
